history_summaries: Round 1: Fix ackA_implies_sel_A failure (DUT bug). Root cause: Controller READY->BUSY transition unconditionally asserted ackReg even when arbiter selection had changed (sel→X because pass_token dropped, making active=0). Fix: In READY state, guard the BUSY/ack transition with `when(isSelected)` — if still selected, proceed to BUSY and assert ack; otherwise fall back to IDLE and set passTokenReg=true to release the token. This re-verifies the selection is still valid before granting ack, closing the 2-cycle pipeline mismatch. All three ack_implies_sel assertions (A/B/C) are fixed since they share the same Controller module. Assertion labels preserved unchanged.

Round 2: Fix liveness_reqA_ackA failure (DUT bug). Root cause: Controller used a 2-cycle pipeline (IDLE→READY→BUSY) requiring two consecutive cycles of matching selection, but the arbiter changes selection every cycle when active (cycles A→B→C→A). The controller in READY never sees the same selection again and falls back to IDLE, creating livelock — no ack is ever produced. Fix: (1) Change controller to single-cycle pipeline — IDLE→BUSY directly when selected with request, skipping READY. Only one cycle of correct selection needed, matching arbiter behavior. (2) Make ack combinational — io.ack := (state===IDLE) && isSelected && io.req, asserted in the same cycle as the trigger condition, satisfying both liveness_reqA_ackA (immediate ack on trigger cycle, timer never starts) and ackA_implies_sel_A (same-cycle sel=A). (3) In IDLE state, non-selected controllers no longer clear passTokenReg (removed `}.otherwise { passTokenReg := false.B }`), preserving their tokens so active stays high and round-robin arbitration continues fairly. All three liveness assertions (A/B/C) are fixed since they share the same Controller module. All assertion labels preserved unchanged. The ackA_implies_sel_A, ackB_implies_sel_B, ackC_implies_sel_C, mutex_ack, and sel_valid_when_active assertions are also preserved by the single-cycle combinational ack design.

Round 3: Fix liveness_reqB_ackB and liveness_reqC_ackC failures (DUT bug). Root cause: The Controller BUSY state handler only exits BUSY when io.req drops (condition `!io.req`). When the arbiter cycles back to re-select a BUSY client while io.req is still high, the controller is stuck in BUSY with no exit path — the combinational ack `(state===IDLE) && isSelected && io.req` evaluates to 0 because state is BUSY, so no ack is generated. Fix: In the BUSY state handler, add `.elsewhen(isSelected)` to transition back to IDLE when re-selected while still busy with a pending request. This allows the controller to return to IDLE, and on the next arbiter cycle that selects this client (A→B→C→A rotation), the combinational ack fires within the 10-cycle liveness bound. The fix addresses the causal path: the controller was stuck in BUSY preventing the ack condition from ever re-evaluating as true when re-selected. Both liveness_reqB_ackB and liveness_reqC_ackC are homologous (same Controller module, same liveness pattern) and are fixed together. All assertion labels preserved unchanged.
